test_title: PYST 14: SSC MTS 2024 - Numerical and Mathematical Ability (Held On: 14 Oct, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A hemispherical container of total surface area 7392 cm² is filled with oil. However, 1/4 of the container is empty. This oil is to be transferred in small hemispherical bottles having radius of 6.3 cm. How many bottles will be required (rounded off to the nearest whole number)? (Take π = (22)/(7))
solution:
**Given:**

Total surface area of hemispherical container = 7392 cm²

The container is 3/4 filled with oil

Radius of small hemispherical bottle (r) = 6.3 cm

**Formula used:**

Surface area of hemisphere = 3πr²

Volume of hemisphere (V) = (2/3)πr³

**Calculations:**

3πR² = 7392

⇒ 3 × (22/7) × R² = 7392

⇒ R² = 784

⇒ R = √784 = 28 cm

Volume of oil in the container = (3/4) × (2/3)πR³

⇒ Volume of oil = (3/4) × (2/3) × (22/7) × 28³

⇒ Volume of oil = (22/7) × 28 × 28 × 14

Volume of one small bottle = (2/3)πr³

⇒ Volume of one small bottle = (2/3) × (22/7) × 6.3³

Number of bottles required = Total volume of oil / Volume of one small bottle

⇒ Number of bottles = [(22/7) × 28 × 28 × 14] / (2/3) × (22/7) × 6.33

⇒ Number of bottles ≈ 66

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
